title: xpute manifest
description: A program's manifest, or one of its protocols: the memory, stack, packet room and GPU its core asks for (manifest.json), or the commands one protocol carries (a protocol file). xpute-gen writes from them both ends' code: MANIFEST, the fields of each `export` command by its number and a handler per `import` command on the runtime, and on the core MANIFEST, a function per `import` command and a trait for the `export` commands. xpute's own protocols (spec/abi/sys.json, spec/abi/gpu.json, spec/abi/fs.json) are protocol files too.

gen.description: Where a file's code goes, each from this file's directory: its TypeScript (a protocol's enums in a folder named as it is, beside it) and its Rust (a manifest's constants, which the core's build script also includes as it links).

mem.description: The memory the runtime gives the core, which never grows.

bytes.description: The sizes a runtime may give, any one of them, each a whole number of regions. The program picks one; the module is linked against the smallest.

region_bytes.description: What a reservation is counted in.

min_heap_bytes.description: The heap the smallest size must leave past the front, the linker's data and the program's fixed ranges, checked as the core compiles.

module_bytes.description: A module's stack, first in the memory.

thread_bytes.description: A native core's thread's stack, outside the memory.

bytes.description: The most bytes a frame's packet takes, either way: a multiple of 8, and at least a stop report with its file path left out, 136 bytes (xpute-core io/door.rs `ABORT_PKT_BYTES`).

fs.description: The file device the core asks for (spec/abi/fs.json), which the runtime attaches and backs with the program's storage. Absent, none, and a file command is refused ENODEV.

stream.description: A stream past the front's frames, which the core writes records into and something beside it runs.

gpu.description: What the core asks of its GPU, read by the GPU plugin.

features.description: WebGPU's feature names. The surface's format is the platform's, and the limits the adapter's.

optional.description: What it takes where the adapter has it.

name.description: A protocol's word for itself, for the generated names only.

export.description: What the core implements and the runtime calls: what the runtime sends the core.

import.description: What the runtime implements and the core calls: what the core posts to the runtime.

extern.description: Types the program's Rust names, read and written as a number.

name.description: Any but Command, which xpute makes from out and in.

unknown.description: The member a number nobody gave out reads as.

val.description: Its number, the wire's and fixed: `major << 8 | minor` where the table names majors. One number space holds every protocol's commands: majors 0x00 to 0x0F are xpute's own, and a program's protocol gives none of them nor a number another of its protocols gives.

pkt.description: Its packet's fields, in order; none, no packet.

call.description: The sender waits for the answer: an `export` the runtime calls, an `import` the runtime answers before the core goes on.

ackreq.description: Posted with ACKREQ and answered later, never waited for. An `import`, its tag the core's: the runtime completes it on a later turn with a frame of the same tag and command flagged RES, its result and `reply`'s packet. An `export`, its tag the runtime's: the core replies as it applies it, with its result.

named.description: An `ackreq` export's reply names the core's memory that holds its answer, which goes with the reply's frame, and the UI's request resolves with a copy of it.

reply.description: An `ackreq` import's completion's packet, its fields in order.

tag.description: What an import's tag carries, which the core gives and its handler is handed before its packet, as a file's descriptor.

mem.description: An import's two fields that name the core's memory, where it is and how long: a runtime hands a UI apart from the core a copy.

type.description: u8, u32, i32, f64, bool, str, or an enum, extern or record named here.
